items.text: **The cube has a third look: the room.** With the field in front, the cube steps wall, floor, room. In the room you sit in the middle, front is up, and sounds can move all the way around you, which is what four or more speakers are for. The room was there before but the cube looked the same as the wall; now it turns orange, shows you as a dot in the middle, a ring around you and four speakers at the corners. Grid in front stays yellow, field green, room orange.

**Scrolling zones in pop-ups no longer slide sideways.** The Index's pin and grip buttons hang 6 px past the card's edge, and a finger could still drag the whole list that far left and right, so the last sections seemed to jiggle. The Index, the Record and Share sheets and the other pop-up lists now hold still sideways.

**Soniscale™ in your words.** The Index entry under Air and Space and the credits now describe it as: a real-time resource engine that decides when individual notes need to be transformed into textures at the same pitch, balancing the player intention, the ear of the listener, and the system capacity.

**A notch never sits on a pill's curved end.** The check that flips a notch away from the curve treated every button in a pill as sitting in both curves (the pill's radius was never limited to half its height), so a notched button at the end of a pill kept its notch on the curve. It now flips to the flat side. Next keeps its notch top left.

**Branding on every size.** A 16:9 capture of a portrait screen had no branding: the frame dropped it on wide shapes. Now every size (screen, 16:9, 4:5, 1:1, 9:16, still, GIF and video) carries your corner mark top right and the CHAMY·XYZ word lower left, as in Current. The picture steps aside if it would touch the corner mark. **Clean** still removes all of it.

**A preview of the size before you shoot.** The Record and Share sheets show the real frame, branding and all, live, with what the size is for (YouTube, Instagram feed, stories, reels, TikTok) and its pixels.
**Fade in and Fade out have icons** (a rising and a falling line) so you can tell the two rows apart.
**Post the link** (Share sheet): X, Bluesky, Threads, Facebook, LinkedIn, Reddit, WhatsApp, Email, as in Current. Instagram and TikTok take the file itself, so save it first.

**Fade in and fade out for video.** The Record sheet has two new rows on Video: **Fade in** (none, .5 s, 1 s, 2 s; default .5 s) and **Fade out** (none, 1 s, 2 s, 4 s; default 2 s). The sound rises at the start instead of starting at full level, and falls over the length you choose; a second tap on stop ends at once. With a fixed length, the fade finishes at that length.

**Notches in the right place.** Next, Air and the line-up button now carry the same top-left notch as the robot and the other pop-up buttons. **Air has a pop-up:** press and hold it for the six cloud looks and the three loop-grain settings; a tap still opens the Air pad.
The undo and redo pill sits a little closer to the bar beside it.

**The dice arrow in the Grain halo now does something.** Tap the small arrow on the dice square and choose **With main dice** (this note rolls its own dice every time the score's dice roll, including Auto) or **By hand** (only when you tap its dice). By hand is the default; a note that is tied shows a ring round its dice square.

**A video ends on your mark.** When you stop (or the time runs out), the picture and the recorded sound fade to black, the Dimitry Saïd Chamy lockup fades in, Dimitry and Chamy move apart, Saïd falls away, all three leave the frame and CHAMY·XYZ appears. It adds about five and a half seconds. Tap stop again to end at once.
**Branding on or off.** A switch in the record and share sheets: CHAMY·XYZ (the word and equalizer under the picture, and the ending) or clean (nothing added). It is remembered.
**Files are numbered:** CHAMY·XYZ_000001, 000002 and so on, in this browser, for videos, GIFs, pictures, sound and notes.
**Steadier sound while recording a video.** The frame is now drawn 30 times a second instead of at every screen refresh (up to 120 on some iPads), which was the likely cause of the crackle you heard.
